deferred_follow_up: Retained passkey credential and challenge replay classification has real mutation evidence, but credential-theft defense remains DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP. The in-memory and SQLite nonce stores now share one retained-key classification seam; focused tests prove first-use acceptance, repeat-use rejection, credential isolation, atomic contention handling, and SQLite reopen persistence. This run does not prevent a compromised authenticator or issuer account from producing a fresh valid assertion, prove every clustered issuer uses the same durable store, qualify relying-party and origin configuration, establish revocation propagation latency, or implement account recovery. Follow-up work must qualify clustered durable-store adoption, phishing-resistant origin policy, rapid revocation, credential replacement, and recovery operations.
note: Real partial mutation evidence. The conformance test at crates/tooling/chio-conformance/tests/threats/passkey_credential_theft.rs records one credential and challenge pair as Fresh and requires its second presentation to return Replayed while a distinct credential remains independent. The in-memory and SQLite stores share retained_replay_outcome for this security decision. A targeted cargo-mutants run replaced that classifier with None at nonce_store.rs:81; the repeated-presentation assertion caught the fail-open replay bypass. PARTIAL: fresh assertion abuse, clustered durable-store adoption, origin policy, revocation latency, and account recovery remain deferred.
